Using the fact that $3=\frac{3}{1},$ we can write the expression as

$$
\frac{3}{1}+\frac{2}{a}.
$$

 

In order to add the two fractions, we need them to have a common denominator. So, we put both fractions over a common denominator of $a$ by multiplying the top and bottom of the first fraction by $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{1}+\frac{2}{a} & = \\ \frac{a}{a}\cdot \frac{3}{1}+\frac{2}{a} & = \\ \frac{3a}{a}+\frac{2}{a}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we add the fractions and simplify the result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3a}{a}+\frac{2}{a} & = \\ \frac{3a+2}{a}\end{aligned}
$$
